G285629.description: Hawally (Arabic: حولي) is an area in, and the namesake of, the Hawalli Governorate, located in the State of Kuwait. Hawally is a large settlement and the commercial center for most computer-related goods in Kuwait.

G285663.description: Bayan (Arabic: بيان) is a residential area and district in the Hawalli Governorate of Kuwait, consisting of 13 blocks, and situated approximately 15 kilometres away from the core areas of Kuwait City. Its naming was inspired by the fact that it is in an area of higher altitude in comparison to its surrounding Mishref, Salwa, and Rumaithiya.

G285704.description: Salmiya (Arabic: السالمية, romanized: As-Sālmīya(h)) is an area in Hawalli Governorate in Kuwait. Salmiya is administratively divided into 12 blocks.

G285726.description: Rumaithiya (Arabic: الرميثية, Gulf Arabic: l-irmēθīya) is a mainly-residential area in Hawalli governorate and a suburb of Kuwait City. It is divided into twelve blocks.

G285728.description: Riqqa (Arabic: الرقة) is an area in Ahmadi Governorate in southern Kuwait. In 2007 it had a population of 56,554.

G285760.description: Wafra (Arabic: الوفرة) is the southernmost area in Kuwait, within the boundaries of the former Saudi–Kuwaiti neutral zone. It is part of Ahmadi Governorate, and is well known for its fertile soil and farms.

G285778.description: Mangaf (Arabic: المنقف) is an area of Kuwait in the Ahmadi Governorate, east of the town of Ahmadi, on the coast of the Persian Gulf and south of Kuwait City. The area has a large concentration of shops and restaurants called Al Azeeziya including a link of the Sultan Center chain.

G285782.description: Mahboula (Arabic: المهبولة, lit. 'mad woman') is a Kuwaiti district on the Persian Gulf, 36 kilometres (22 mi) south of Kuwait City. It is located in the Ahmadi Governorate between the areas of Fintās and Abu Halifa.

G285787.description: Kuwait City ( ; Arabic: مدينة الكويت, romanised: Madīnat al-Kuwayt) is the capital and largest city of Kuwait. Located at the heart of the country on the south shore of Kuwait Bay on the Persian Gulf, it is the political, cultural and economic primate city of the emirate, being home to the headquarters of most Kuwaiti corporations and the entirety of its banking system.

G285799.description: Al Jahra (Arabic: الجهراء) is an area located 32 kilometres (20 mi) west of the centre of Kuwait City in Kuwait. It is the capital of the Al Jahra Governorate of Kuwait as well as the surrounding Al Jahra District.

G285810.description: Funaitees (Arabic: الفنيطيس) is an area located in the governorate of Mubarak Al-Kabeer in Kuwait. The name in Arabic means "water tanks", referring to the freshwater tanks carried on ships that historically arrived in the area to supply freshwater to various parts of Kuwait.

G285811.description: Fahaheel is an area in Kuwait, located in the Ahmadi Governorate in the country's south. Located on the coast of the Persian Gulf, it lies east of the Ahmadi area.

G285812.description: Al Fintas (Arabic: الفنطاس) is an area located in the Ahmadi Governorate, Kuwait. A suburb located to the south of Kuwait City, Al Finţās has about 23,000 inhabitants, and is situated at 29.17° North latitude, 48.12° East longitude.

G285815.description: Farwaniya (Arabic: الفروانية, Gulf Arabic: /ɪlfərwaːniːjə/) is an area of Farwaniya Governorate, located within the agglomeration of Kuwait City, Kuwait. The Ghazali Expressway passes to the west of the district and the road leading to Kuwait International Airport to the east, both roads in a north–south direction.

G285839.description: Al Ahmadi (Arabic: الأحمدي) is an area in Kuwait, and the capital of Al Ahmadi Governorate. It was founded in 1946 with the discovery of oil there.

G285856.description: Dasma (Arabic: الدسمة) is one of the areas of the Capital Governorate in Kuwait City, Kuwait. Its name, literally translated to 'Rich', is in reference to its rich soil and numerous historical wells.

G387958.description: Salwa (Arabic: سلوى) is an area in Hawalli Governorate in Kuwait City, Kuwait, bordering Rumaithiya to the north, Bayan and Mishref to the west, Messila to the south and the Persian Gulf to the east. It had the first zoo in Kuwait, established in 1954, which closed and relocated to the Kuwait Zoo in 1968.

G387994.description: Al Murqab (Arabic: المرقاب) is an area in Kuwait City, Kuwait. It is located in the Capital Governorate 8 miles (13 km) from Kuwait International Airport.

G412800.description: Sabah Al-Salem (Arabic: صباح السالم) is an area in the Mubarak Al-Kabeer Governorate of Kuwait. As of 2022, its population is 139,163, spread out over 13 blocks.

G7329411.description: Mubarak Al-Kabeer City (Arabic: منطقة مبارك الكبير) is an area in Kuwait. The Mubarak Al-Kabeer governorate is named after the area.
